Know Your Competitor: F19

Same battlefield, different playbook. Get familiar with the European rival matching IRIS CARBON deal for deal in CSRD and ESEF reporting.

🎯

F19 Digital Reporting is a Netherlands-based platform built around the "last inch" of corporate reporting — the final stretch where a finished report has to become a compliant, published, multi-format document. It shows up in the same conversations IRIS CARBON does, especially with EU-listed and Dutch organisations working through CSRD and ESEF.

This module walks through their actual product demo, lines their platform up against ours feature by feature, and gives you the talk track for when a prospect says "we're also looking at F19."

Who is F19?

F19 Digital Reporting is a Netherlands-based software company (Eindhoven) building a cloud platform for CSRD, ESEF, and SBR (Dutch Standard Business Reporting) compliant corporate reporting. Their pitch is squarely about the final, complex stage of reporting: taking finished content and turning it into a compliant, multi-format publication without manual rework.

HQ
Eindhoven, Netherlands
Regulatory focus
CSRD, ESEF, SBR
Positioning
"The last inch" of reporting
Output formats
Website, PDF, XHTML, iXBRL, InDesign
💬 Straight from their own marketing
"Streamline the last inch in corporate reporting with F19, the digital-first, multichannel publishing platform."

Their whole story is built around that phrase — the "last inch" being the gap between a finished Word/Excel draft and a compliant, published, on-brand report.

Confirmed reference clients: KPMG Netherlands, Arcadis, Alliander, FMO, Port of Rotterdam, CZ.

F19 vs IRIS CARBON

Same problem, two different companies solving it. Know exactly where the lines are before a prospect asks.

⚖️
DimensionF19 Digital ReportingIRIS CARBON
Primary marketNetherlands / Benelux-heavyGlobal — 30+ regulatory authorities, five continents
Regulatory focusCSRD, ESEF, SBR (Dutch)SEC/EDGAR, CSRD/ESRS, BRSR, FERC, and more
Output formatsWebsite, PDF, XHTML, iXBRL, InDesigniXBRL, PDF, web-based disclosure
AI-assisted taggingNot shown — manual taxonomy tree taggingIRIS Niti: AI-powered iXBRL tagging
Approval workflowPer-article remarks + validate/approve/publish gatesRole-based workflow across the suite
Design/print outputDirect InDesign exportNot a native output format
🤝 Where we're similar
Both are cloud-based, single-source reporting platforms built around iXBRL tagging for CSRD/ESEF compliance, with block-based content editors and multi-format publishing from one place.
✅ Where IRIS CARBON pulls ahead
Regulatory breadth beyond Europe (US SEC, India BRSR, FERC), AI-assisted tagging through Niti, and a larger, more geographically spread client base.
⚠️ Where F19 pulls ahead
Direct InDesign export for print-quality annual reports, rich media (video) embedded natively inside published report pages, and deep, specific support for Dutch SBR.

One Source, Five Outputs
Publishing
Embedded video reports. Report pages can carry a native video block, not just a link out. In the demo, a Sustainable Development Goals video sits directly inside a Continuous Reporting page — published straight to the live website alongside the surrounding text and charts, no separate media player needed.
InDesign export. Same source content, one click away from a print-ready InDesign file. Design teams and agencies can pick up the layout without a manual re-key — alongside the website, PDF, XHTML, and iXBRL exports generated from that same source.
Taxonomy & tagging tree. A dedicated Taxonomy tab lets a preparer browse the full ESEF element tree — assets, non-current assets, property/plant/equipment, equity, liabilities — and apply a tag directly onto text or figures inside the article. It's manual, but visible and auditable line by line.
Word & Excel sync. Existing Word documents import through a 5-step wizard — Upload, Options, Cut, Verify, Menus — that turns each into a structured, taggable article. An "ExcelSync" feature keeps live financial tables in step with the source spreadsheet instead of a one-time paste.
Built-in approval workflow. Every article carries its own remarks thread plus three role-gated checkpoints — Prepare for validation, Approve for publication, Publish article — each assignable to a specific role, like Administrators.
One source, five outputs. Upload once — Word, Excel, images, video, slides — and publish to iXBRL, a responsive website, XHTML, PDF, and InDesign, all from the same CMS, without re-keying content per channel.

Screen 4 · Where We Win

Read The Room Before You Walk In

F19's own client list tells you exactly who they're strong with — and where that leaves room for us.

🏆
📍 Their footprint
Every confirmed F19 client — KPMG Netherlands, Arcadis, Alliander, FMO, Port of Rotterdam, CZ — is a Dutch organisation. That's a real, credible base, but it's a single-country base. It's the first thing to listen for on a call.

Tap each claim to see the counter 👇

True, and a genuine strength worth acknowledging. But the real question is regulatory breadth, not output count — ask what happens the day their client also needs a US SEC or India BRSR filing.
Point to Niti — AI-assisted iXBRL tagging plus historical period comparison. Manual tagging trees scale badly once filing volume grows across multiple entities and reporting cycles.
That's real, and worth respecting on a call. It's also a tell: their playbook is built around one filing regime. Ask how they'd support a global group with US, India, or multi-jurisdiction reporting needs.
Good proof they're credible in the Netherlands. It also means most of their reference stories won't travel outside Benelux — useful context if your prospect operates across multiple regulatory geographies.
